home.h1: Hand the things you repeat on your Mac every day to Keyboard Maestro
lead: Keyboard Maestro is a Mac automation app from Stairways Software. You tell it when and what: press this key and open that app, type these few letters and swap in a whole paragraph. Once you've told it, it does the job in the background, the same way every time. This site is for people who have never automated anything, and for people who already use it and want to go further.
, not affiliated with Stairways Software. For features and how they work, the official wiki is the source of truth.
home.ctaNote: Lesson 1 builds a key that opens an app, lesson 2 turns a few letters into a whole paragraph, and lesson 3 makes one key run your start-of-day routine. No code needed.
PAIN: Answering parents, customers or colleagues, you type "Got it, thanks, I'll get back to you by Friday" letter by letter several times a day.
Every morning you open Mail, Calendar and the same web page, then drag each window back where it belongs before you can start.
There's a menu command you use every day that has no shortcut, so every time you go hunting for it with the mouse.
Every job application or quote means copying the same intro and the same contact details out of the last one.
You copy something important, then copy something else, and the first thing is gone for good.
Every evening at the same time you're meant to open the same spreadsheet and log your parents' blood pressure, and on busy days you forget.
home.lessonsP: Read them in order. Each takes ten or fifteen minutes and you build as you go. After these three you can make your own macros, and everything else on the site is there to look up when you need it.
home.tracksP: After a few macros you'll want it to do more. The full guide runs in 8 steps, roughly along three tracks. Start with whichever one you need right now.
TRACKS: Macro groups decide where a macro works, triggers decide when it starts, and actions say what it does. Understand those three and you can build most macros yourself.
Remember some text, ask you a question, take a different path depending on what's happening, wait for something before carrying on. And get back anything you've copied.
When it misfires, and going further
When a macro doesn't work, check permissions and the Engine first, then step through to see where it gets stuck. Later, hook in scripts, use the same macros on two Macs, and share macros with others.
home.tracksLabel: Matching steps in the full guide
YES: There's something you do on your Mac several times a day and you'd like to hand it off
You don't write code. The three beginner lessons don't need a single line
You're willing to spend a few minutes granting it system permissions like Accessibility, since it presses keys, chooses menus and moves windows for you
You want to try before you decide. It's paid software, and the official site has a fully working trial
NO: You're not on a Mac. It's Mac only and needs macOS 10.13 or later
You don't want to give any app system permissions. Without them, many macros can't run
It's a one-off job. Doing it once by hand is quicker
